title: The Whale That Traded Its Legs for the Ocean 😱
script: A 50-ton animal once walked on four legs — and we have the bones to prove it. Pakicetus, a wolf-sized mammal in 50-million-year-old Pakistan, waded into rivers chasing fish. Over eight million years, its nostrils crept backward, its legs shrank to flippers, and its hips disconnected from its spine entirely. That hip bone still floats loose inside every modern whale — a leftover leg with nowhere to go. Eight million years to trade a forest for an ocean. Could you give up everything familiar for a completely different world?
search_summary: Pakicetus was a four-legged land mammal 50 million years ago that evolved into modern whales.
comment_question: A floating hip bone inside every whale — why hasn't evolution removed it yet? 🤔

title: The Cuttlefish That Hypnotizes Prey With Its Own Skin 😱
script: It flashes hypnotic waves across its skin — and the crab just freezes. That's a cuttlefish hunting. It fires rippling pulses of light called 'passing clouds' directly at prey, overloading their nervous system. The crab locks up, cuttlefish strikes. It rewrites its own skin pattern 50 times per second — faster than any screen you own. Zero ink, zero noise, just light — and dinner is done. If you could flash any signal to freeze an enemy, what would it say? And that's why.
search_summary: Cuttlefish use hypnotic skin patterns called passing clouds to paralyze and stun prey before striking.
comment_question: Is this the most terrifying hunting trick in the ocean? 😳
source_note: Wood et al., Journal of Experimental Biology, 1994
